content:
Looking at the folds: the octagon is folded along vertical, horizontal, and diagonal lines through opposite vertices, producing an 8-layer triangle whose corners correspond to the center, a "axis" vertex, and a "diagonal" vertex of the octagon.

The cut removes the corner at the axis vertex, perpendicular to the fold line running from the center to that vertex. Unfolding, this cut is replicated by all the fold symmetries: each of the four axis vertices (top, bottom, left, right) gets sliced off by a straight cut, while the four diagonal vertices remain as corners.

The result is a shape with four long flat sides (from the cuts) and four clipped corners — i.e., a square-like outline with cut corners.
